"""PyDESeq2 Wald test, treated vs control, design ~ batch + group (from tpl-pydeseq2-two-group@1.0.0, extended output)."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats

np.random.seed(0)
ALPHA = 0.05

raw = pd.read_csv("/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-counts/counts.tsv", sep="\t", index_col=0)
symbols = raw["symbol"]
counts = raw.select_dtypes("number").T
samples = pd.read_csv("/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-meta/samples.csv", index_col=0, dtype=str).loc[counts.index]
# filter: >=10 counts in >=3 samples (smallest group size)
counts = counts.loc[:, (counts >= 10).sum(axis=0) >= 3]

dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts, metadata=samples, design="~ batch + group")
dds.deseq2()
stats = DeseqStats(dds, contrast=["group", "treated", "control"], alpha=ALPHA)
stats.summary()
res = stats.results_df.copy()  # unshrunk Wald estimates

out = pd.DataFrame({
    "gene": res.index, "symbol": symbols.reindex(res.index).values,
    "base_mean": res["baseMean"].values, "log2_fold_change": res["log2FoldChange"].values,
    "pvalue": res["pvalue"].values, "adjusted_pvalue": res["padj"].values,
}).sort_values("adjusted_pvalue")
out.to_csv("output/de_results.csv", index=False)

sig = out.adjusted_pvalue < ALPHA
summary = pd.Series({
    "genes_tested": len(out), "padj_na": int(out.adjusted_pvalue.isna().sum()),
    "significant": int(sig.sum()), "up": int((sig & (out.log2_fold_change > 0)).sum()),
    "down": int((sig & (out.log2_fold_change < 0)).sum()),
    "sig_abs_log2fc_gt1": int((sig & (out.log2_fold_change.abs() > 1)).sum())})
summary.to_csv("output/de_summary.csv", header=["value"])
print(summary)

plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
d = out.dropna(subset=["adjusted_pvalue"]).copy()
d["y"] = -np.log10(d.adjusted_pvalue.clip(lower=1e-300))
s = d.adjusted_pvalue < ALPHA
ax.scatter(d.log2_fold_change[~s], d.y[~s], s=6, c="#bbbbbb", label="padj >= 0.05")
ax.scatter(d.log2_fold_change[s], d.y[s], s=8, c="#31688e", label="padj < 0.05")
ax.axhline(-np.log10(ALPHA), ls="--", c="k", lw=.7)
for x in (-1, 1):
    ax.axvline(x, ls=":", c="k", lw=.7)
for _, r in d.nsmallest(10, "adjusted_pvalue").iterrows():
    ax.annotate(r.symbol, (r.log2_fold_change, r.y), fontsize=6, xytext=(3, 3), textcoords="offset points")
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change (treated / control)")
ax.set_ylabel("-log10 adjusted p-value")
ax.set_title(f"Treated vs control (Wald, n=3 v 3): {int(s.sum())} genes FDR<0.05")
ax.legend(fontsize=7)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("figures/volcano.png", dpi=300)
fig.savefig("figures/volcano.pdf")

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import anndata as ad
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats

np.random.seed(0)
ALPHA = 0.05

raw = pd.read_csv("/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-counts/counts.tsv", sep="\t", index_col=0)
symbols = raw["symbol"] if "symbol" in raw.columns else pd.Series(raw.index, index=raw.index)
counts = raw.select_dtypes("number").T
samples = pd.read_csv("/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-meta/samples.csv", index_col=0, dtype=str).loc[counts.index]
# filter: >= 10 counts in >= 3 samples (smallest group size)
counts = counts.loc[:, (counts >= 10).sum(axis=0) >= 3]
print("genes kept", counts.shape[1], "of", raw.shape[0])
print("library sizes", counts.sum(axis=1).to_dict())

dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts, metadata=samples, design="~ batch + group")
dds.deseq2()
stats = DeseqStats(dds, contrast=["group", "treated", "control"], alpha=ALPHA)
stats.summary()
res = stats.results_df.copy()   # unshrunken Wald LFC, p and padj
unshrunk_lfc = res["log2FoldChange"].copy()
stats.lfc_shrink(coeff="group[T.treated]")
res["log2FoldChange"] = stats.results_df["log2FoldChange"]  # shrunken LFC for reporting/plot; p and padj are from the Wald test

out = pd.DataFrame({
    "gene": res.index, "symbol": symbols.reindex(res.index).values,
    "log2_fold_change": res["log2FoldChange"].values,
    "log2_fold_change_unshrunken": unshrunk_lfc.values,
    "pvalue": res["pvalue"].values, "adjusted_pvalue": res["padj"].values,
    "base_mean": res["baseMean"].values})
out.to_csv("output/de_results.csv", index=False)
sig = out.adjusted_pvalue < ALPHA
print(len(out), "tested;", int(sig.sum()), "significant;",
      int((sig & (out.log2_fold_change > 0)).sum()), "up;", int((sig & (out.log2_fold_change < 0)).sum()), "down")
print(out.sort_values("adjusted_pvalue").head(10).to_string())

# PCA on top 500 variable genes
norm = np.log2(np.asarray(dds.layers["normed_counts"]) + 1)
top = np.argsort(norm.var(axis=0))[::-1][:500]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4))
for g, c in [("control", "#440154"), ("treated", "#FDE725")]:
    for b, m in [("1", "o"), ("2", "s")]:

ax.set_title("PCA, top 500 variable genes"); ax.legend(fontsize=7)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("figures/pca.png", dpi=300); fig.savefig("figures/pca.pdf"); plt.close(fig)

# AnnData + normalized CSV
A = ad.AnnData(X=np.asarray(dds.layers["normed_counts"]), obs=samples.copy(), var=pd.DataFrame(index=counts.columns))
A.layers["counts"] = counts.values
o = out.set_index("gene").reindex(A.var_names)
for c in o.columns:
    A.var[c] = o[c].values
A.write_h5ad("output/de_results.h5ad")
pd.DataFrame(A.X.T, index=counts.columns, columns=counts.index).to_csv("output/normalized_counts.csv")

# Volcano
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
y = -np.log10(out.adjusted_pvalue.clip(lower=1e-300))
ax.scatter(out.log2_fold_change[~sig], y[~sig], s=6, c="#9a9a9a", label=f"n.s. ({int((~sig).sum())})")

ax.axhline(-np.log10(ALPHA), ls="--", c="k", lw=0.8); ax.axvline(0, ls=":", c="k", lw=0.8)
for i in out.sort_values("adjusted_pvalue").head(10).index:
    ax.annotate(out.symbol[i], (out.log2_fold_change[i], y[i]), fontsize=6, xytext=(3, 3), textcoords="offset points")
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change (treated vs control, shrunken)"); ax.set_ylabel("-log10 adjusted p-value")
ax.set_title("Treated vs control (PyDESeq2 Wald, ~ batch + group)"); ax.legend(fontsize=7)

- Batch is balanced across groups (each group has two batch-1 samples and one batch-2 sample), so including it costs little and does not confound the contrast.
- The gene filter was ≥10 counts in ≥3 samples, matching the smallest group size.
- The template applies apeglm shrinkage to the fold changes.

## Design (samples.csv)
- 6 samples: treated T1–T3 and control C1–C3, with 3 biological replicates per group.
- Batch column: T1, T3, C1 and C3 are in batch 1. T2 and C2 are in batch 2. Each group has one sample in batch 2, so batch is balanced across groups and can be modelled as a covariate.

- All 120 lines use **kit A**.

- **Kit lot** differs on every line. It rises one at a time from 1000 (line 1) to 1119 (line 120).
- **PCR cycles** run through 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26 and then repeat. The cycle length is 7, so each count appears 17–18 times in the 120 lines.

## How the cells were treated (protocol.md)
- Every line treats the cells with **compound X**. The text does not name the cell line or cell type, the vehicle, or the culture conditions. It does not describe a control (vehicle-only) treatment.

- **Duration** cycles through 6, 7, 8 h, a cycle of 3.
- Dose and duration together repeat every 12 lines, so there are 12 distinct dose × time combinations (5–8 µM × 6–8 h). Each combination appears 10 times in the 120 lines.

## Caveats for the analysis
1. **No sample mapping.** Both files have 120 lines, but the study has 6 samples (3 treated, 3 control). We cannot tell which lot, PCR cycle count, dose or duration belongs to which sample.

## Suggested next step
Ask for a table with one row per sample and columns for kit lot, PCR cycles, dose, duration, and vehicle for controls. Until then, treat batch as a possible covariate in differential expression and report the treatment effect with that caveat.
